title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J.K. Rowling
description: A young orphaned wizard discovers his magical heritage on his eleventh birthday and attends Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, embarking on an epic adventure against dark forces.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable home-loving hobbit, is persuaded by the wizard Gandalf and thirteen dwarves to journey across Middle-earth to reclaim treasure guarded by the dragon Smaug.

title: A Game of Thrones
author: George R.R. Martin
description: Noble families vie for control over the Iron Throne of Westeros in a brutal political and magical conflict while an ancient supernatural threat awakens in the northern wilderness.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: The tale of Kvothe, an infamous wizard, musician, and adventurer, recounting his childhood in a troupe of traveling players and his education at an arcane university.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: Set on the desert planet Arrakis, young Paul Atreides must navigate political treachery, giant sandworms, and prophecy to secure the universe's most precious resource, the spice melange.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: Mathematician Hari Seldon develops psychohistory to predict the fall of the Galactic Empire and creates an intellectual foundation at the edge of the galaxy to preserve human civilization.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: A washed-up computer hacker in a dystopian cyberspace future is hired by a mysterious employer for one ultimate cyber heist against an artificial intelligence.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: An astronaut stranded alone on Mars uses botanical engineering, scientific ingenuity, and humorous perseverance to survive until a rescue mission can reach him.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: An accessible exploration of how Homo sapiens evolved from foraging apes into rulers of the earth through cognitive revolution, agricultural expansion, and scientific progress.

title: Guns Germs and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
description: A transdisciplinary historical analysis examining why Eurasian civilizations conquered others through geographical, environmental, and technological advantages rather than genetic superiority.

title: India After Gandhi
author: Ramachandra Guha
description: A detailed historical narrative of modern Indian democracy, conflicts, politics, cultural diversity, and nation-building following independence in 1947.

title: The Discovery of India
author: Jawaharlal Nehru
description: Written during imprisonment, this book traces the philosophical, cultural, artistic, and social history of India from the Indus Valley Civilization to the freedom movement.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
description: The definitive biography of the visionary Apple co-founder whose relentless passion for perfection and technological design revolutionized personal computing, music, and mobile phones.

title: Wings of Fire
author: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
description: An inspiring autobiography of India's Missile Man and former President, chronicling his early struggles in Rameswaram, his career in ISRO and DRDO, and his vision for Indian youth.

title: The Wright Brothers
author: David McCullough
description: The dramatic story of Wilbur and Orville Wright, two bicycle mechanics from Dayton Ohio who changed the world through mechanical ingenuity and human flight.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Master detective Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John Watson investigate a supernatural ghostly hound terrorizing a wealthy family on the foggy moors of Devonshire.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description: Ten strangers are invited to an isolated island mansion off the English coast, only to be accused of murder and systematically eliminated according to a sinister nursery rhyme.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
description: Symbologist Robert Langdon investigates a cryptic murder in the Louvre Museum, uncovering hidden codes in Leonardo da Vinci's paintings and a centuries-old secret society.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet navigates manners, social standing, family drama, and romantic misunderstandings with the haughty and wealthy Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy in 19th-century England.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Bronte
description: An orphaned governess finds employment at Thornfield Hall and falls in love with the brooding Mr. Rochester, only to discover dark secrets lurking in his ancestral manor.

title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A classic software engineering guide for programmers on writing readable, maintainable, modular code with effective naming conventions, functions, and unit testing practices.

title: Python Crash Course
author: Eric Matthes
description: A hands-on, project-based introduction to Python programming for beginners, covering data structures, functions, web development, data visualization, and game building.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen
description: The comprehensive standard university textbook on computer algorithms, data structures, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, and computational complexity analysis.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig
description: The leading authority textbook exploring artificial intelligence fundamentals, search algorithms, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, and robotics.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow and Yoshua Bengio
description: A comprehensive theoretical and practical foundation for deep learning, artificial neural networks, backpropagation, convolutional networks, sequence modeling, and generative models.

title: Natural Language Processing with Python
author: Steven Bird and Ewan Klein
description: A practical guide to analyzing natural human language text using the Python programming language and the Natural Language Toolkit NLTK library.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: A proven framework for building good habits and breaking bad ones through tiny changes, 1 percent improvements, habit stacking, and behavioral psychology.

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
description: A spiritual guide to mindfulness, transcending egoic thought patterns, living in the present moment, and achieving internal peace and psychological freedom.

title: Thinking Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: Nobel laureate explores the two mental systems that drive how we think: System 1, fast and emotional; and System 2, slow, deliberate, and logical.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Set in the American South during the Great Depression, lawyer Atticus Finch defends an innocent black man accused of rape while his young daughter Scout learns about empathy.

author: George Orwell
description: A chilling dystopian novel depicting totalitarian government surveillance under Big Brother, psychological manipulation, propaganda, thoughtcrimes, and censorship.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: A tragic portrait of the Jazz Age, decadent wealth, obsession, disillusionment, and the fleeting American Dream on Long Island through the enigmatic Jay Gatsby.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: An inspirational philosophical story of an Andalusian shepherd boy named Santiago who journeys to the Egyptian pyramids in search of a hidden treasure and his personal legend.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: A poetic scientific journey through the universe, human curiosity, astronomical discoveries, the evolution of galaxies, and mankind's place in the cosmic expanse.

title: Silent Spring
author: Rachel Carson
description: A landmark environmental science book exposing the dangers of synthetic pesticides and sparking the modern ecological and conservation movement.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
description: A candid coming-of-age story of teenage alienation, identity struggle, and rebellion in New York City as told by Holden Caulfield.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andrew Hunt and David Thomas
description: Essential software career advice on clean design, debugging techniques, automated testing, continuous learning, and pragmatic software craftsmanship.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: An in-depth guide examining storage engines, distributed consensus, data replication, streaming pipelines, and reliability in scalable modern architectures.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: A powerful memoir of a woman who leaves her isolated survivalist family in rural Idaho to pursue higher education, earning a PhD from Cambridge University.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: A psychological thriller about a famous painter who inexplicably shoots her husband in the face and never speaks another word, and the psychotherapist determined to unravel her secret.
